definition: In linguistics, a triphone is a sequence of three consecutive phones.
details: Triphones are useful in models of natural language processing where they are used to establish the various contexts in which a phoneme can occur in a particular natural language.

explainer.lead: A triphone is three consecutive phones, used to describe the context in which a phoneme occurs. It matters because speech changes with neighbouring sounds, so context-sensitive units model real pronunciation better than isolated phonemes.

tiers.eli5: A sound rarely comes out the same every time; a triphone looks at a sound plus the one before and after, like judging a person by the company they keep.
tiers.practitioner: Speech engineers build triphone-based acoustic models so each phoneme is modelled in its left and right context; the pitfall is combinatorial explosion, since the number of possible triphones is very large.
tiers.paperLevel: A triphone is a sequence of three consecutive phones, used to establish the various contexts in which a phoneme can occur in a given natural language.

explainer.example: In the word 'cat', the /a/ sound is modelled as the triphone /k/-/a/-/t/.
